This process begins with monitoring inventory levels in a warehouse or store.
When stock reaches a predefined threshold, an automated alert or manual check signals the need to reorder.
The procurement team then places an order with suppliers, considering factors like cost, delivery time, and supplier reliability.
Once the order is placed, the inventory system updates with expected delivery dates.
Upon receiving the stock, it is inspected for quality, recorded in the system, and placed on shelves or in storage.
The process ends when the inventory levels are updated after the restock is complete.

args.text: When a description presents multiple activities that must all be completed after receiving an item, represent the activities as parallel branches and synchronize them before continuing; use an exclusive gateway for alternatives.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing documented guideline already covers modeling required concurrent activities and alternatives.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use a parallel join when a shared continuation waits for all active parallel branches. Never use it to join mutually exclusive alternatives.
Use an inclusive split when one or more conditions can be true; use an inclusive join to synchronize only activated reachable branches.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.

args.text: When a process description lists multiple required activities after an event, model them as parallel branches if they are independent, and synchronize the branches before a shared continuation.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers the missing split and synchronization structure.

result.rule: When When a description names multiple distinct activities within one phase and states that the process continues only after every activity is finished,: model the activities as parallel branches with a parallel split and join, rather than as a sequence.

When the description states distinct decisions or approvals at different points in the process: Model each decision or approval at the point stated, and connect it to the activities that precede and follow it in the described order; do not replace one decision with another.
When the description says an activity may take place before a later activity: Model the optional activity as a decision branch with a path that bypasses it; merge the paths before the later activity.

When the description states that the process begins when an incoming communication or request occurs, without describing separate work to receive it: Represent that occurrence with a suitable start event; model a separate receipt activity only when the description states that receiving it is work to be performed.

args.text: When the description lists multiple required, independent activities in one phase and indicates that a later step waits for them to be complete, model them as parallel branches with a parallel split and join before the shared continuation; model mutually exclusive choices separately, not as parallel work.
